candidate.description: Force-only ppps lowering using three-root interpolation, explicit one-dimensional TRR/HRR state programs, one shell task per lane, shared density weights, and the existing persistent exact-class queue ABI.

correctness.host_oracle: Every ppps component value and all four-center gradients agree with the independent subset/Wick oracle; center D is recovered by translation invariance.

limitations: The CUDA emitter is force-only and specialized to ppps; the backend-independent state planner is generic.
No production Fock emitter was built because the lower-order force prototype already failed the resource and timing gates.
No five-root dddd interpolation table or CUDA root evaluator was added.
The microbenchmark retains the production queue ABI but does not constitute the 192-AO endpoint gate.

decision.reason: The low-order ppps prototype is 2.27x to 2.89x slower than the production component-lane recurrence and compiles at 255 registers per thread with stack traffic and spills. Scaling the same lowering to five-root, 1296-component dddd cannot satisfy the zero-spill or 10% endpoint promotion gates without a materially different cooperative design.
